blazers.pulse: Rip City is riding a 6-1 start after road wins in Denver and Phoenix, and the road record is still perfect. The buzz got dented when Vit Krejci fractured his lower left leg against the Suns, leaving the backcourt thin heading into tonight's game at the Lakers.
storylines: Won 132-119 at Phoenix on Wednesday: Lillard had 25, Clingan had his best offensive night of the season (24 pts, 11 reb, 3 blk).
Beat Denver 118-110 on Monday behind Deni Avdija's 28, with Toumani Camara's late three sealing it.
Krejci fractured his lower left leg taking a charge; he's out tonight and coach Micah Nori says surgery hasn't been decided.
With Sharpe, Morant and Krejci all out, Lillard, Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday carry the guard minutes.

timbers.pulse: The 3-1 home win over Houston on Sunday pulled Portland back into an eighth-place Wild Card spot, so the playoff fate is in their own hands. It all comes down to Decision Day at Austin tomorrow.
storylines: Beat Houston 3-1 on Nov. 1: David Da Costa and Kristoffer Velde scored, and Vincent Janssen added the insurance goal after Houston pulled one back.
A win at Austin on Saturday clinches a third straight playoff berth, in Martí Cifuentes' first season in charge.
A draw is enough only if Colorado loses at Dallas.
A win guarantees at least a Wild Card spot, and seventh place (a direct Round One berth) is still possible.

f1.pulse: Kimi Antonelli is now F1's youngest-ever champion after finishing third in Mexico City, where Max Verstappen took the win. The bigger talking point is Ferrari's civil war after Hamilton and Leclerc tangled for the lead and threw away a likely win, and the circus heads to Interlagos this weekend.
storylines: Antonelli, 20, clinched the title in Mexico: first Italian champion since Ascari in 1953 and Mercedes' first drivers' crown since 2020.
Ferrari row: Hamilton said a teammate 'worked against' him, Leclerc got a 5-second penalty, and Vasseur scolded both for a lack of respect.
Mercedes can wrap up the constructors' title in Brazil by outscoring Ferrari by three points or more.
Rafael Câmara makes his F1 debut for Haas at his home race, replacing Esteban Ocon; no sprint this weekend.
